title: Memory models
examples: What is the difference between short-term and working memory?
Can you explain the multi-store model in more detail?
How does working memory help us learn new things?

explain.say: Today we are looking at how our memory works in your brain.
The multi-store model suggests memory has different parts working together.
The sensory store briefly holds information from our senses for a split second.
The short-term store can hold a small amount of information for a short time.
Long-term memory stores information for much longer periods, potentially forever.
Working memory is more active; it uses information for thinking right now.

faq.q: How is working memory different from short-term memory?
faq.a: Short-term memory is just a temporary holding space for information. Working memory is more active because it involves manipulating that information to solve problems.
asks: What is the difference between STM and WM?
Does working memory do more than just remembering?

faq.q: Does the multi-store model explain everything about memory?
faq.a: No, many modern theories suggest memory is more complex than just these separate stores. It suggests these systems interact constantly.
asks: Is the multi-store model completely accurate?
Are there other models we should know about?

faq.q: If I forget something, is it because my LTM failed?
faq.a: Forgetting can happen at any stage. You might fail to encode it into the STM, or you might not retrieve it from LTM.
asks: Why do I forget things I know?

faq.q: How much information can my short-term memory really hold?
faq.a: The classic estimate suggests it can hold about seven plus or minus two pieces of information at one time.
asks: What is the limit of our short-term memory?
Can I remember more than seven things?

faq.q: What is the role of attention in memory?
faq.a: Attention is crucial because it acts as a filter. You must pay attention to information for it to enter the short-term store effectively.
asks: Do I need to pay attention to remember things?

facts: The multi-store model proposes three stages: sensory, short-term, and long-term memory.
The short-term store has a limited capacity, often cited as around seven plus or minus two units.
Working memory is responsible for the active processing and manipulation of information currently being thought about.
Encoding information correctly is vital for moving it from short-term to long-term memory.

quiz.say: If you briefly see a flash of light, which store processes that initial sensory input?
quiz.why: The sensory store captures raw input from your senses for a very brief moment.

wrong.1: The short-term store holds information you actively focus on, not just fleeting sensory data.
wrong.2: The long-term store is for permanent memories, not instant sensory flashes.
wrong.3: Working memory uses the information, it is not the initial recording mechanism itself.

quiz.say: Which memory system is best described as the 'mental workspace' for current thought?
quiz.why: Working memory is the active system where you manipulate ideas, like calculating in your head.

wrong.0: The long-term store is for storage, not for the real-time processing of thoughts.
wrong.2: The sensory store only holds raw, unprocessed sensory data briefly.
wrong.3: While related, working memory implies active use, which is more than just holding data.
